info.title: openbuild demo data
info.description: Demo data covering every schema this app supplies, offered as the first step of the app's setup walkthrough. Generated from the schemas themselves, so every object satisfies the schema that will validate it.

x-openregister.description: Demo data for openbuild. NOT installed automatically — a mock register is imported on demand, from the setup walkthrough or `occ openregister:descriptors:list --app=openbuild --import=<slug>`.

buildiq.title: OpenBuild Register (demo)
buildiq.description: Demo data for OpenBuild Register. Generated from the register's own schemas — see hydra-gates/scripts/lib/generate_mock_register.py.

Application.title: Application
Application.description: An app built or customized with OpenBuild (unify-apps-with-app-type). The `appType` discriminator distinguishes a `virtual` app (fully delivered by OpenBuild) from a `hybrid` app (a delta layered over an installed Nextcloud fleet app, linked via `baseRef`). Per ADR-002 the Application carries identity (slug, name, description, appType, baseRef, permissions) plus a productionVersion relation to the ApplicationVersion currently exposed at the canonical URL. Manifest, semver, and lifecycle live on ApplicationVersion. For a hybrid app the identity metadata (slug/name) mirrors the underlying NC app and is read-only after creation (enforced by HybridMetadataLockListener).

slug.title: Application Slug
slug.description: Kebab-case slug; uniquely identifies the virtual app within its organisation. Drives the runtime path /builder/{slug}/*. Max 48 chars so the synthetic appId `openbuild-{slug}` fits NC appId caps (per design.md OQ-4). READ-ONLY on a hybrid app (it mirrors the installed Nextcloud app it customizes) — enforced by HybridMetadataLockListener + the abstract data widget's x-openregister-readonly-when honouring. A `-dark` suffix is RESERVED and rejected by the pattern: it would collide with the dark-variant icon route /icons/{slug}-dark.svg (a `foo-dark` app's light-icon request matches the dark route first), silently breaking that app's icon resolution (see appinfo/routes.php icon#iconDark/iconLight ordering; SlugValidator::RESERVED_APP_SLUG_SUFFIX).

name.title: Application Name
name.description: Human-readable name displayed in the OpenBuild shell. READ-ONLY on a hybrid app (mirrors the installed app) — enforced server-side + reflected by the data widget.

description.title: Application Description
description.description: Optional long-form description of the app. READ-ONLY on a hybrid app (mirrors the installed app) — enforced server-side + reflected by the data widget.

appType.title: Application Type
appType.description: IMMUTABLE once created (layered-versioned-app-deltas) — enforced server-side by HybridMetadataLockListener and rendered read-only by the abstract object data widget (CnObjectDataWidget honours `readOnly`). The unified-app discriminator (unify-apps-with-app-type). `virtual` = an app fully delivered by OpenBuild (its ApplicationVersion manifest is built from scratch or from a template). `hybrid` = an app that customizes an already-installed Nextcloud fleet app (opencatalogi, pipelinq, …) — its ApplicationVersion carries a delta-only manifest layered over that fleet app's bundled manifest, served raw via GET /api/app-overrides/{appId} and merged client-side. An Application with no `appType` is treated as `virtual` on read (legacy default). Purely declarative — the Apps-list filter and the Virtual/Hybrid badge read this field directly (no Service).

status.title: Publication Status
status.description: Publish status that gates the per-app Nextcloud top-bar navigation entry. `draft` (default) = work-in-progress, hidden from the app menu. `published` = live, listed in the menu by AppNavigationService (which filters Applications on `status == published`). `archived` = retired. Flipped via the explicit Publish / Unpublish owner action (POST /api/applications/{appUuid}/publish|unpublish). MUST be a declared property so OpenRegister persists it — an undeclared status is stripped on save.

baseRef.title: Base Reference
baseRef.description: Optional link to the base this app extends. For a `hybrid` app `baseRef.kind` is `fleet-app` and `baseRef.id` is the kebab-case Nextcloud app id of the installed app being customized (the canonical link used by the /api/app-overrides/{appId} shim and the all/virtual/hybrid filter). For a `virtual` app `baseRef` MAY be absent. Mirrors the per-version baseRef shape from the app-delta-override model.

kind.title: Base Kind
kind.description: What kind of base the app extends — `fleet-app` for a hybrid app customizing an installed Nextcloud app.

id.title: Base Identifier
id.description: Identifier of the base — for a hybrid app, the installed Nextcloud app id (e.g. `opencatalogi`).

manifestVersion.title: Base Manifest Version
manifestVersion.description: Optional version of the bundled base manifest the delta was authored against, so a stale delta is diagnosable.

productionVersion.title: Production Version
productionVersion.description: Relation → ApplicationVersion currently exposed at the canonical /apps/openbuild/{slug} URL. READ-ONLY on a hybrid app (its production version is the admin-managed shared delta) — enforced server-side + reflected by the data widget. Set explicitly by the admin (creation wizard, detail-page version switcher), not derived from chain terminality. The referenced ApplicationVersion's `application` relation MUST point back at this Application — enforced server-side by ApplicationVersionService::guardProductionVersionOwnership() (ADR-031 §Exceptions(1) cross-row guard).

icon.title: Light Mode Icon
icon.description: Optional top-level light icon reference. Points to an SVG file attached to the Application record via OR files-attached-to-object (ADR-001). Sibling to manifest — not inside it. Drives the /icons/{slug}.svg endpoint (REQ-OBICON-002).

ref.title: Icon File Reference
ref.description: Filename of the SVG file attached to this Application record.

iconDark.title: Dark Mode Icon
iconDark.description: Optional top-level dark icon reference. Points to an SVG file attached to the Application record via OR files-attached-to-object (ADR-001). Sibling to manifest — not inside it. Drives the /icons/{slug}-dark.svg endpoint (REQ-OBICON-003).

ref.title: Dark Icon File Reference
ref.description: Filename of the dark-mode SVG file attached to this Application record.

allowUserOverrides.title: Allow User Overrides
allowUserOverrides.description: Per-app permission flag (layered-versioned-app-deltas). When true, users of this app MAY create/edit their own user-scoped manifest delta layered over the admin delta (base ⊕ admin ⊕ user). Default false (default-secure) — an Application with no allowUserOverrides reads as false. Read directly by the override resolver, ApplicationVersionOwnerGuard, and the dashboard 'create override' affordance; purely declarative (no Service).

permissions.title: Access Permissions
permissions.description: Per-Application RBAC block per REQ-OBRBAC-001 (openbuild-rbac). Each entry is a principal — either a Nextcloud user UID (prefix `user:<uid>`) or a Nextcloud group GID (prefix `group:<gid>` OR bare value, kept for back-compat). The caller is granted access when their UID matches a `user:` entry in any role OR when their group memberships intersect a `group:`/bare entry in any role. Bare strings continue to mean GID for backwards compatibility with pre-#37 manifests. owners gate destructive actions (publish, archive, delete, transfer, permissions edit); editors gate save; viewers gate read.

owners.title: Owners
owners.description: Principals with owner role (full control including publish/archive/delete/transfer-ownership/edit-permissions). Each entry is a `user:<uid>`, `group:<gid>`, or bare group GID.

editors.title: Editors
editors.description: Principals with editor role: can save manifest drafts but cannot publish or change permissions. Each entry is a `user:<uid>`, `group:<gid>`, or bare group GID.

viewers.title: Viewers
viewers.description: Principals with viewer role: read-only access. Each entry is a `user:<uid>`, `group:<gid>`, or bare group GID.

githubRepo.title: GitHub Repository
githubRepo.description: Optional linkage to the app's round-trip GitHub home (github-app-repo-format REQ-OBA-010). Set by the owner round-trip capability (github-app-sync) when the app is linked/pushed; omittable so every existing Application stays schema-valid. Purely declarative (stored data, no state machine, no calculation) per ADR-031 — read by the shop + sync surfaces, populated by no runtime that never touches GitHub.

owner.title: Repository Owner
owner.description: GitHub owner (user or organisation) of the linked repository.

name.title: Repository Name
name.description: GitHub repository name of the app's round-trip home.

githubDefaultBranch.title: GitHub Default Branch
githubDefaultBranch.description: Optional branch that push/pull operations target, resolved from the linked repo's default branch at link time and admin-overridable (github-app-repo-format REQ-OBA-010). Omittable; purely declarative per ADR-031.

dataRegisters.title: Data Registers

register.title: Register Slug
register.description: Slug of the shared OpenRegister register this app binds to (e.g. `spectr`). Unlike ApplicationVersion.register, this register is NOT owned or provisioned by Buildiq and carries NO `buildiq-` prefix convention — it is an existing register OpenConnector or another process feeds independently.

label.title: Display Label
label.description: Optional human-readable label shown in the builder's data-source pickers instead of the raw register slug (e.g. `Spectr market intelligence data`). Purely a UI convenience; absent falls back to the raw slug.

dataRegisters.description: Shared, non-versioned OpenRegister registers this Application binds to alongside its own per-version register (ADR-002 `ApplicationVersion.register`). Declared per SPECTR-NEXTCLOUD-PLAN.md §4.2 / hydra ADR-050 decision #2. Version promotion (`VersionPromotionService`) never reads or writes this property — it operates exclusively on `ApplicationVersion.register` — so promoting a version neither copies nor migrates any row in a data register. Sibling to `baseRef` on the `Application` schema; absent on every Application created before this property existed.

connectors.title: Connectors
connectors.description: OpenConnector configuration objects this application explicitly declares as its own. Exported into `connectors/<kind>/<slug>.json` by app-repo-format-v2 so an installed app arrives with the ingestion that populates the registers its pages read. Declared entries are exported as declared; the exporter additionally resolves the objects a declared entry DIRECTLY references (one level only — a synchronization's source, mapping and target), because a synchronization without its source installs into something that cannot run. Credential VALUES are never exported: configs carry credential references only, and any inline secret-shaped value is stripped and the strip recorded.

kind.title: Connector Kind
kind.description: Which OpenConnector schema the entry refers to. Constrained to the four configuration kinds that define ingestion; `endpoint` and `rule` are deliberately excluded — an endpoint is instance-facing surface and a rule belongs to the automations channel.

uuid.title: Connector UUID
uuid.description: UUID of the OpenConnector object in the shared `openconnector` register. The binding is UUID-keyed, NOT slug-keyed, because OpenConnector objects overwhelmingly have no slug: measured on a live instance, only 13 of 369 sources, 1 of 291 mappings, 7 of 206 synchronizations and 0 of 74 jobs carry one, while every object has a UUID. A slug-keyed binding could therefore reference almost none of a real app's ingestion — the export would silently collect nothing. Validated as a UUID BEFORE it is ever used as a path component, so a crafted value cannot escape the `connectors/<kind>/` prefix on export.

slug.title: Connector Slug
slug.description: OPTIONAL human-readable slug. Used as the exported filename when present and safe (`connectors/<kind>/<slug>.json`), because a slug is far more reviewable in a diff than a UUID; the export falls back to the UUID when absent. Never used for resolution — the UUID is the identity.

label.title: Label
label.description: Optional human-readable label for the binding, shown in the builder. Never used as a path component.

flows.title: Flows

flow.title: Flow UUID
flow.description: UUID of the OpenRegister flow this app is composed of, resolved against the OpenRegister `Flow` ENTITY (OCA\OpenRegister\Db\FlowMapper::findByUuid) — the store the flow engine actually executes. ⚠️ UUID and NOT the numeric `id`: an id is an auto-increment column, per-instance, and would resolve to a different flow or to nothing after an export; a UUID is globally unique and survives the trip provided the importing side seeds the flow with the same one, which the follower spec requires. The `Flow` entity carries uuid/name/app and NO slug, so there is no slug to bind by. ⚠️ An `agentflow` OBJECT store in the hermiq register mirrors some definitions and drifts from the entity: a definition written to the object left the engine executing the previous graph, with the run log showing the old node set and no error surfaced anywhere. Consumers MUST resolve the entity. Per ADR-065 there is exactly ONE flow engine, in OpenRegister; a flow that calls an agent is an ORDINARY flow whose nodes are agentic node types contributed to the engine's registry by hermiq (`hermiq.workload-step`, `hermiq.workload-collect`), not a separate kind of object, and it binds through this property like any other flow.

label.title: Display Label
label.description: Optional human-readable label shown instead of the raw UUID (e.g. `Hydra sequencer`). A UUID is unreadable in a picker, so this matters more here than it does for a slug-addressed binding; absent falls back to the flow's own name.

sourceUuid.title: Source UUID
sourceUuid.description: OPTIONAL. Set only when this binding was created by applying a published `flows/` channel entry (app-repo-format-flow-agent-export). Carries the UUID the flow was PUBLISHED under on the source instance — never the same as `flow` on this instance, because a fresh install mints its OWN flow UUID through `FlowService::save()` rather than seeding the published one (that entry point stamps `owner`/`organisation` and rebuilds the trigger index; a raw insert at a caller-chosen UUID would have to reimplement both by hand). Re-applying the same published repository checks THIS property, not `flow`, so a repeat pull is idempotent rather than duplicating the flow on every run. Absent on every binding authored directly in the builder.

flows.description: OpenRegister flows this Application is composed of. Read by the export so an exported app carries the flows that make it do anything; absent means the app binds none. A binding whose UUID resolves to nothing MUST NOT make the Application invalid — deleting a flow is ordinary — and is reported by the consumer rather than dropped at write time. There is deliberately no sibling `agents` binding: agents already point at their application via `agent.applicationSlug`.

rules.description: A hybrid app MUST carry a baseRef.id naming the installed Nextcloud app it customizes (unify-apps-with-app-type). Same-row rule; the cross-row metadata-lock (slug/name immutable on hybrid) is enforced imperatively by HybridMetadataLockListener (ADR-031 §Exceptions(1) cross-row).
rules.message: A hybrid app requires baseRef.id (the installed Nextcloud app it customizes).

ApplicationTemplate.title: Application Template
ApplicationTemplate.description: A pre-baked starter pack for building an Application from a recognisable use case — manifest plus companion schemas. Seeded Conduction-curated templates carry isSeeded: true. Per the hybrid register model this schema is shared across the `openbuild` register; cloned user schemas land in a per-app `openbuild-{slug}` register.

slug.title: Template Slug
slug.description: Kebab-case unique slug for the template.

title.title: Template Title
title.description: Human-readable title (plain English) shown in the gallery.

description.title: Template Description
description.example: Municipal building-permit workflow with index, detail, form, and kanban pages.

useCase.title: Use Case
useCase.description: Short one-line label describing the use case (plain English).

category.title: Category
category.description: Top-level category used for filtering in the gallery.

screenshotUrl.title: Screenshot URL
screenshotUrl.description: Relative path under the app's img/templates/ folder, or an OR Files URL.

manifest.title: App Manifest
manifest.description: Full app-manifest JSON blob (ADR-024) to be deep-copied on clone.

companionSchemas.title: Companion Schemas
companionSchemas.description: JSON-schema blobs to be cloned alongside the manifest into the user's per-app register (openbuild-{slug}).

isSeeded.title: Is Seeded
isSeeded.description: True for Conduction-shipped templates, false for org-local templates.

sourceUrl.title: Source URL
sourceUrl.description: Link back to the originating user-story / RFP / blog post for traceability.

version.title: Template Version
version.description: Semver version of the template — recorded on clone for one-shot snapshot semantics.

ApplicationVersion.title: Application Version
ApplicationVersion.description: A deployable runtime for an Application (ADR-002). A VIRTUAL app's version carries a full `manifest` blob and owns its own per-version OpenRegister register so production and test data are physically isolated. A HYBRID app's version (unify-apps-with-app-type) instead carries a delta-only customization: `manifest` is an empty object `{}`, `baseRef.kind` is `fleet-app`, and `manifestDelta` holds the keyed structural diff served raw via GET /api/app-overrides/{appId} and merged client-side over the installed fleet app's bundled manifest (OpenBuild holds no fleet base). The admin-defined linear promotion chain reads via the optional `promotesTo` relation. Lifecycle (draft → published → archived) is per-version; the `draft → published` transition upserts the BuiltAppRoute slug index.

name.title: Version Name
name.description: Human-readable display label set by the admin (e.g. `Production`, `Staging`, `Development`).

slug.title: Version Slug
slug.description: URL-safe kebab-case slug for this version (e.g. `production`, `staging`, `development`).

manifest.title: App Manifest
manifest.description: JSON manifest blob conforming to @conduction/nextcloud-vue/src/schemas/app-manifest.schema.json (v1.4.0+). Per ADR-024, this is consumed by useAppManifest + CnAppRoot at runtime. Per ADR-002 the manifest now lives on ApplicationVersion (was on Application). For a HYBRID app's version this is an empty object `{}` — the customization lives in `manifestDelta` and is merged client-side over the installed fleet app's bundled manifest (unify-apps-with-app-type).

manifestDelta.title: Manifest Delta
manifestDelta.description: Keyed structural manifest delta (unify-apps-with-app-type), set ONLY on a HYBRID app's version. Produced by @conduction/nextcloud-vue's diffManifest and consumable by mergeManifestDelta (pages keyed by page.id, widgets by widget.id, the { "$op": "remove" } deletion marker, the optional `__order` reorder key). Served raw via GET /api/app-overrides/{appId} and merged CLIENT-SIDE over the fleet app's bundled manifest, because OpenBuild does not hold the fleet app's base. Absent on virtual apps (which carry a full `manifest`).

baseRef.title: Base Reference
baseRef.description: Optional link to the base this version's delta extends (unify-apps-with-app-type / app-delta-override). For a HYBRID app's version `baseRef.kind` is `fleet-app` and `baseRef.id` is the installed Nextcloud app id. Lets base drift be diagnosed when a fleet app rebuilds and renames/removes a page the delta targeted.

kind.title: Base Kind
kind.description: What kind of base the delta extends — `fleet-app` for a hybrid app's version.

id.title: Base Identifier
id.description: Identifier of the base — the installed Nextcloud app id for a hybrid app's version.

manifestVersion.title: Base Manifest Version
manifestVersion.description: Optional version of the bundled base manifest the delta was authored against.

register.title: Data Register
register.description: Per-version OpenRegister register name carrying this version's schemas and objects. Convention: `openbuild-{appSlug}-{versionSlug}` (e.g. `openbuild-hello-world-production`). Actual provisioning is owned by the creation-wizard capability (sibling spec).

semver.title: Semantic Version
semver.description: Semantic version of this ApplicationVersion. Initial value `0.1.0`. Patch-bumped automatically by ApplicationVersionService::onSave() when the manifest content changes (SHA-256 of canonicalised manifest differs from the previously-stored hash). Metadata-only edits do NOT bump semver. Minor/major bumps remain manual.

status.title: Lifecycle Status
status.description: Per-version lifecycle state. Driven by x-openregister-lifecycle below.

application.title: Parent Application
application.description: Relation → parent Application (required). Real first-class OR relation, not a UUID string (ADR-002 §Decision).

promotesTo.title: Promotes To
promotesTo.description: Optional relation → next ApplicationVersion in the linear promotion chain. Terminal versions have `promotesTo: null`. Cycle detection is enforced server-side by ApplicationVersionService::guardNoCycle() (ADR-031 §Exceptions(1) cross-row).

scope.title: Delta Scope
scope.description: Delta scope discriminator (layered-versioned-app-deltas). `admin` (default) = the instance-wide shared delta managed by admins (today's behaviour — the only existing scope). `user` = a per-user delta owned by a single user, layered over the admin delta and resolved as `base ⊕ admin ⊕ user` only when the parent Application's allowUserOverrides is true. An ApplicationVersion with no scope reads as `admin` (legacy default). Read by ApplicationVersionOwnerGuard + PermissionResolver + the override resolver; admin/user rows share this one schema (no new schema). On a `user` row the per-version promotion/publish fields (semver/status/promotesTo/register) are inert — the user delta is just manifestDelta + owner + baseRef.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: Owning Nextcloud user UID. Set ONLY on a `scope: user` row; identifies the single user who may read/edit/rollback this user-scoped delta. Empty/absent on `scope: admin` rows. Read by ApplicationVersionOwnerGuard + PermissionResolver for the user-scope ownership check (a user can never read/write another user's delta — fail-closed).

commitSha.title: GitHub Commit SHA
commitSha.description: Optional GitHub provenance (github-app-repo-format REQ-OBV-112). The exact Git commit this version was pushed to (on publish to GitHub) or pulled from (on import). Omittable; absent on versions with no GitHub provenance. Purely declarative per ADR-031 — a commitSha write is metadata and does NOT by itself bump `semver` (the manifest-content auto-bump, REQ-OBV-103, is unaffected).

sourceRef.title: GitHub Source Ref
sourceRef.description: Optional GitHub provenance (github-app-repo-format REQ-OBV-112). The branch/tag/ref a PULLED version was imported from (e.g. `refs/heads/main` or a tag name). Omittable; absent on versions with no GitHub provenance. Purely declarative per ADR-031 — no lifecycle or semver effect.

rules.description: Same-row self-loop guard: an ApplicationVersion cannot promote to itself. Broader cross-row cycle detection lives in ApplicationVersionService::guardNoCycle().
rules.message: promotesTo cannot equal the version's own UUID (self-loop).

rules.description: A user-scoped delta MUST name its owner UID (layered-versioned-app-deltas). Same-row rule; the cross-row owner-vs-caller authorization is enforced imperatively by ApplicationVersionOwnerGuard + PermissionResolver (ADR-031 §Exceptions(1) cross-row).
rules.message: A user-scoped ApplicationVersion requires an owner UID.

draft.description: Editable working version, not exposed at the canonical `/apps/openbuild/{slug}` URL unless this version is the parent Application's productionVersion.

published.description: Reachable through routing — eligible to be the parent Application's productionVersion. The on_transition action upserts the corresponding BuiltAppRoute keyed by the parent Application's slug.

archived.description: No longer reachable. Preserved for restore via the `reopen` transition.

publish.description: Mark this version as ready to be the parent Application's productionVersion. Relocated from Application schema per ADR-002 — published-ness is per-version now. Authorization (REQ-OBRBAC-004): owner of the parent Application (or a Nextcloud admin) only — enforced by the ApplicationVersionOwnerGuard `requires` tag below, which OR's LifecycleValidationListener runs on this transition.

archive.description: Retire a published version. Operators are responsible for swapping the parent Application's productionVersion off this row first. Authorization (REQ-OBRBAC-004): owner of the parent Application (or a Nextcloud admin) only — enforced by ApplicationVersionOwnerGuard.

reopen.description: Restore an archived ApplicationVersion to draft for further editing. Authorization (REQ-OBRBAC-004): owner of the parent Application (or a Nextcloud admin) only — enforced by ApplicationVersionOwnerGuard.

BuiltAppRoute.title: Built App Route
BuiltAppRoute.description: Index from slug → applicationUuid. Maintained by the Application lifecycle (upserted on publish, deleted on archive). Used by the runtime to resolve /builder/{slug} → manifest in a single OR lookup. Per ADR-022 this is an explicit flattened index rather than scanning the Application collection.

slug.title: Route Slug
slug.description: Matches the Application slug. Unique within the organisation (enforced by lifecycle upkeep + 4xx on conflict).

applicationUuid.title: Application UUID
applicationUuid.description: UUID of the published Application this route resolves to.

HelloMessage.title: Hello Message
HelloMessage.description: Seed schema for the canonical hello-world virtual app. Three sample messages are seeded on install so the install is testable out of the box.

exportJob.title: Export Job
exportJob.description: Asynchronous pipeline that turns a published Application into a standalone Nextcloud app — delivered as a ZIP download or pushed to GitHub. Lifecycle is declarative per ADR-031; the file-generation surface is an ADR-031 §Exceptions(3) imperative path.

applicationUuid.title: Application UUID
applicationUuid.description: UUID of the source Application record being exported.

applicationVersion.title: Application Version
applicationVersion.description: Semver of the Application version being exported.

target.title: Export Target
target.description: Delivery target — ZIP download or push to a new GitHub repository.

status.title: Job Status
status.description: Lifecycle state. Transitions are enforced by OR's lifecycle engine.

githubRepo.title: GitHub Repository
githubRepo.description: Target GitHub repository name (only when target=github).

githubVisibility.title: GitHub Visibility
githubVisibility.description: Visibility for the new GitHub repository (only when target=github).

githubRepoUrl.title: GitHub Repository URL
githubRepoUrl.description: URL of the created GitHub repository (populated on success when target=github).

githubPullRequestUrl.title: GitHub Pull Request URL
githubPullRequestUrl.description: URL of the placeholder pull request opened against the repo's default branch.

includeSeedData.title: Include Seed Data
includeSeedData.description: When true, exports seed data alongside the schema bundle.

license.title: License
license.description: License chosen by the user for the exported app.

downloadUrl.title: Download URL
downloadUrl.description: Relative URL where the ZIP can be downloaded (only when target=zip).

downloadExpiresAt.title: Download Expiry
downloadExpiresAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp at which the ZIP expires and is purged by the cleanup job.

errorMessage.title: Error Message
errorMessage.description: Human-readable failure reason. Never contains the GitHub PAT (see Decision 3 in design.md).

log.title: Execution Log
log.description: Ordered list of progress entries. Never contains the GitHub PAT.

dataRegisters.title: Data Registers

register.title: Register Slug
register.description: Slug of a register named in the source Application's `dataRegisters`, as declared at export-submission time.

includeData.title: Include Row Data
includeData.description: When true, the export additionally bundles this register's current row data as a reference fixture alongside its schema definitions (which are always bundled). Defaults to false (schema definitions only).

dataRegisters.description: Per-export choice of which of the source Application's `dataRegisters` bindings to bundle, and whether to include each one's row data. Export-flow state persisted on the ExportJob record by ExportJobService::queue() — not Application configuration. Absent on every ExportJob created before this property existed; ExportJobService::queue() defaults it to [].

githubCredentialId.title: GitHub Credential
githubCredentialId.description: UUID of the `github` credential in OpenRegister's credential broker to push with (only when target=github). A reference, never a token: Buildiq sends {method, path, body} plus this UUID to the broker, which checks ownership, the allowed-app grant and the allow-rules, then injects the secret. Buildiq cannot read the secret behind it.

requestedBy.title: Requested By
requestedBy.description: Nextcloud UID of the user who queued the export. Carried so the session-less background job can tell the broker which identity owns `githubCredentialId` — the broker's owner/IDOR guard needs an identity, and a cron run has no session to read one from.

applicationSlug.title: Application Slug
applicationSlug.description: Slug of the source Application, captured at submission time by ExportJobService::queue() from the route parameter. RunExportJob reads it back to build the export context (appId, appNamespace, appName) and to resolve the agents that point at this application via `agent.applicationSlug`. Persisted on the job rather than re-derived from applicationUuid because the export runs as a background job, long after the request, and the slug is the identity the exported app is BUILT with — re-resolving it later would let a renamed Application change the appId of an export already in flight.

flows.title: Flows

flow.title: Flow UUID
flow.description: UUID of an OpenRegister flow named in the source Application's `flows` bindings, as chosen at export-submission time. Resolved by FlowAndAgentExportBundler against the OpenRegister `Flow` ENTITY (FlowMapper::findByUuid) — the store the engine executes — and NOT against the `agentflow` object mirror, which drifts from it. A UUID and not the numeric `id`: an id is a per-instance auto-increment column and would resolve to a different flow, or to nothing, on the importing instance.

flows.description: Per-export choice of which of the source Application's `flows` bindings to bundle. Export-flow state persisted on the ExportJob record by ExportJobService::queue() (via sanitiseFlows(), which keeps only `flow` and drops the builder-UI `label`) — not Application configuration; the Application's own binding lives on Application.flows, declared in 22-flows-and-agents.json. Absent on every ExportJob created before this property existed; ExportJobService::queue() defaults it to [].

queued.description: Newly created; waiting to be picked up by the worker.
